threatModel.summary: Current authorized repository HEAD 4e10eca69c42211651ca907f38b74b6d19e6928c implements an in-process Rust DOCX comparison, edit, inspection and PDF/PNG rendering engine, exposed through native CLI, Python/PyO3, WASM Node/browser APIs and Node CLI. Python MCP serves document tools over stdio. Bindings disable engine defaults, enabling shared CLI grammar without native self-update. Native rendering additionally accesses host fonts/cache. Release and AI-review workflows exercise separate network/publication authority. No hosted document service or tenant deployment was established (src/lib.rs:7-30; jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:35-40; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-32; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381).
assets: Confidential document bytes, revisions/deleted text, comments, metadata, images/fonts, projections and rendered outputs; caller memory, local files and MCP responses carry these assets (src/lib.rs:17-30; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:126-150,185-218).

Source/output integrity and edit intent: optional legacy source_sha256 guard, prepared source/request/output digests, exact anchors and native prepublication source reread (src/edit.rs:2081-2088; src/edit/prepared.rs:196-235; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1642-1655).

Process availability: default admission allows 64 MiB compressed/per-part, 256 MiB total inflation, 10000 entries and depth 256; comparison/WmlDocument allows 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB total (src/admission.rs:63-99; src/wml_document.rs:50-55).

Filesystem authority: MCP retained root and derived out_dir/{clean.docx,redline.docx,patch.diff,report.json}, optional redline.pdf/page PNGs; ambient CLI destinations; native Markdown resource-root image files; system/user/cloud fonts and persistent font index (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185-217; src/publication.rs:146-225; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2858-2878; src/convert/font.rs:2281-2315,3098-3107).

Native executable, release artifacts, optional signing key, GitHub publication tokens, cargo/npm/PyPI credentials and Jules service/token capabilities (.github/workflows/release.yml:230-369; scripts/release.sh:374-380,919,935-954,1069; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:28-50).
trustBoundaries: Untrusted package bytes enter ZIP/XML/DOM and image/font/legacy parsers. Admission checks budgets, header/extent consistency, safe canonical names, duplicate identities, encryption/compression and bounded inflation. Checked XML validates before DOM construction; permissive parse_xdocument deliberately does not enforce policy (src/admission.rs:439-575; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:90-135). Renderer first admits input, normalizes Strict packages, opens PartFs and expands package-contained altChunks (src/convert/mod.rs:769-808).

JSON edit requests cross into mutation: preparation resolves/checks operations and candidate results before returning bytes; legacy SHA-256 guarding is optional, not authentication or approval. Signed/macro-bearing edit packages are refused (src/edit/prepared.rs:196-235; src/edit.rs:2081-2105).

MCP clients share operator --root, default cwd. Startup normalizes root and opens _OutputRoot; actual reads/publication use retained cap-std authority, not merely Python resolve checks. Writes validate relative names, reject output symlinks and require overwrite for conflicts. No tenant separation or human approval is implemented (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; src/publication.rs:146-199,228-250,431-463).

Native CLI publication grants ambient selected-path authority; Python/Node CLI handlers also own ambient host I/O and do not inherit MCP confinement. Native OutputRoot publication is atomic per file, not across the artifact set (src/publication.rs:168-225; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-110).

Native Markdown images use --resource-path or input parent (fallback .), decode escapes, reject URL schemes and require canonical containment plus capability-relative read. Python/Node CLIs reject resource_path (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2878,2937-2943; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:1057-1064; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:724-727).

Native rendering accesses ambient fonts independently of MCP root: macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts; Linux ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/jubarte/fonts; Windows %APPDATA%/jubarte/fonts. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides these. Index defaults to parent(font-directory)/font-index.tsv; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides or empty/off disables it. Cached face paths are read after stamp checks; saves write a sibling filename ending .tsv.<pid>.tmp then rename (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3098-3107,3154-3229).

Explicit native self-update transfers release-publisher authority into executable replacement. Repository/platform/tag, SHA256SUMS.txt and regular-file extraction are configured; RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None leave signature enforcement disabled (src/update.rs:25-48,87-108,186-258,299-321).

Tag-triggered GitHub release consumes build artifacts, optionally signs using step-scoped ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY staged under $RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN with exit cleanup, and publishes dist/* using contents:write. Local release additionally publishes cargo/npm/PyPI packages using operator credentials (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,230-321,356-369; scripts/release.sh:374-380,919,935-954,1069).

Pinned external Jules review and companion-fix actions have distinct authority. Review gets PR/check writes with enable_approve=false. Companion invocation rejects fork heads, requires configured trusted author/dispatcher arthrod and qualifying events, then sets require_plan_approval=false and AUTO_CREATE_PR. External action internals are absent. Self-hosted CI/docs execute repository code under runner authority (.github/workflows/jules-review.yml:17-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:69-92,259-324; .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-48; .github/workflows/docs.yml:76-99).

Verified resource-row details retained from the independent architecture review: native cloud fonts derive from $HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<single-normal-component-family>; renderer and rendered output receive font bytes under OS permissions (src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236). The persistent font index is read by the native renderer/current account and defaults to macOS ~/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv, Linux ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/jubarte/font-index.tsv, or Windows %APPDATA%/jubarte/font-index.tsv; JUBARTE_FONT_DIR changes the default parent and JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX separately overrides/disables it (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3098-3107). Python CLI uses selected Path.write_bytes destinations, Node CLI selected fs.writeFileSync destinations; these recipients are local filesystem readers under operator/OS authority, distinct from MCP OutputRoot (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-110). Updater's selected archive binary path is jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte[.exe], with SHA256SUMS.txt from the fixed repository (src/update.rs:25-48,104-108,198-207). Release private-key values are represented only by the ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY secret reference; the signing step and zipsign process receive temporary key files, then the GitHub publisher receives dist/* through GH_TOKEN using contents:write (.github/workflows/release.yml:261-309,356-369).
attackerCapabilities: Document suppliers control package names/metadata, XML/relationships, embedded media/fonts, legacy structures and Markdown text; host environment, chosen trusted roots, release credentials and operator accounts are not implied capabilities.

MCP clients can read/process under-root documents and invoke exposed writes with overwrite=true. Outside-root access would add authority; ordinary inside-root replacement is already granted (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,153-159).

Local path-race or font-index adversaries require write access to the relevant directories/index. Document-only control does not establish that prerequisite (src/publication.rs:146-148; src/convert/font.rs:3154-3229).

Library callers can select permissive parsing, budgets and callbacks; CLI operators already select ambient paths. These choices become boundaries only when a host exposes them to less-trusted callers.

Release-asset publishers can replace archives and adjacent sums; current checksum-only updater provides no independent signature restriction. PR submitters control review context but lack the configured companion invocation authority unless its gates pass (src/update.rs:44-48,245-249; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324).
securityObjectives: Bound untrusted parsing and preserve safe package identities; callers must additionally enforce process CPU/memory limits (src/admission.rs:439-575; SECURITY.md:38-74).

Avoid document-driven network fetching, macro execution and external office processes; confine native Markdown image reads to the caller-selected resource root (src/admission.rs:16-22; src/lib.rs:7-11; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2878).
Confine MCP document I/O, preserve source/intent guards, require explicit replacement and report partial publication accurately; application root checks are not a process sandbox.
Protect executable/release integrity and secret recipients; keep review verdicts separate from human approval and maintain distinct external-action privileges.
assumptions: No supplied user deployment context/model/knowledge base. Resource paths are configuration-derived expressions; actual runtime environment values, permissions, transport exposure and hosting limits were not supplied.

MCP claims tools only touch root, but native rendering also reads fonts and persists the font index outside that root. Document I/O is confined; process-wide confinement is not established (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:5-9,67-108; src/convert/font.rs:2281-2315,3098-3107,3182-3229).

Signing is explicitly staged in docs; current compiled updater uses checksums only. Workflow signing, if provisioned, does not imply these binaries verify signatures (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80; src/update.rs:44-48,245-249).

SECURITY.md names rdocx-opc 0.2, while consumed manifest dependency is oxml-opc 0.14.2 with quick-xml 0.41/0.42. This is documentation drift, not an advisory finding (SECURITY.md:89-94; Cargo.toml:104-117).
Engine edit refusal is distinct from filesystem publication failure; multi-file commit can be partial (src/publication.rs:168-174).

Remote action internals, self_update dependency internals, actual credentials, registry/tag protections and self-hosted runner isolation remain unverified. Architecture mapping is not audit completion or a vulnerability finding.

findings.title: Rendering a DOCX with an extreme HTML colspan can exhaust process memory
findings.summary: A small internal HTML altChunk can set a cell colspan to billions. Rendering serializes one XML grid column per span before layout, causing excessive CPU and memory use despite archive admission.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document content can terminate the host operation through extreme allocation. Impact is process availability; remote/shared service exposure is not established and process isolation is advised.
severity.changeConditions: Host memory/CPU limits constrain impact to a worker; a shared service processing without isolation increases operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified input propagation, unrestricted usize span parsing and proportional string-writing loop; no runtime reproduction.

codeEvidence.explanation: The output String grows once per attacker-selected column, before DOM or page raster limits can act.

rootCause.summary: The internal chunk loader passes HTML into html_to_wml. Cell colspan values have no maximum; end_table sums them and emits one gridCol into a growing String for each column. Admission bounds original archive content, while this expansion happens afterward without a generated-byte budget.

findings.remediation: Reject excessive per-cell spans and aggregate column counts using checked arithmetic before serialization, and enforce a conversion-wide generated-byte budget.

limitations: No application execution or runtime reproduction.
No deployment or host resource limits supplied.
validation.summary: Parent confirmed the path in current source. A single representable large colspan suffices; the issue does not rely on integer overflow. Initial archive budgets and later page pixel limits do not bound this loop.

impact.why: Process availability loss; no code execution or confidentiality gain established.

likelihood.why: A small HTML numeric value reaches the unbounded growth loop.

reachability.summary: Public conversion and render/report APIs enter with_layout; recipient processing of a supplied document is required, host configuration control is not.

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX containing an internal HTML altChunk table with a very large colspan and induce PDF/PNG rendering or a layout report.

remediationTests: Excessive colspan refuses before grid generation.

findings.title: Rendering malformed WMF images can retain overlapping text copies until memory is exhausted
findings.summary: WMF payload fields are bounded by the whole image rather than their own record. Repeated short records can each copy tens of kilobytes from following records, turning a small embedded image into gigabytes of retained text.

severity.rationale: An untrusted image can exhaust the processing host's memory/CPU. Impact is process availability, with no remote service exposure or code execution established.
severity.changeConditions: Host process quotas contain the failure; shared processing without isolation increases operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified image reachability, whole-buffer field reads, owned text retention and short-record advancement in current source; no runtime reproduction.

codeEvidence.explanation: The image path dispatches bytes to the metafile parser and retains its returned text.

codeEvidence.label: Outer WMF size check
codeEvidence.explanation: The check bounds the record extent but payload reads continue using the entire file.

codeEvidence.label: Both WMF text operations
codeEvidence.explanation: Count-based text and coordinate reads can cross the declared record into following records.

codeEvidence.label: Polygon operations
codeEvidence.explanation: Polygon and polypolygon counts likewise read whole-file data without record-local boundaries.

codeEvidence.label: Polyline and advancement
codeEvidence.explanation: Polyline reads whole-file coordinates while the parser advances only by declared record bytes.

codeEvidence.label: Owned text copies
codeEvidence.explanation: Every accepted overlapping string becomes a distinct retained MetaText allocation.

codeEvidence.label: EMF record-local checks
codeEvidence.explanation: The sibling EMF point reader checks each point against the declared record extent.

rootCause.summary: raster_wmf verifies only that each declared size fits in the remaining file. TEXTOUT and EXTTEXTOUT then resolve count-sized strings and coordinates against data, not a slice of that record, and retain owned MetaText. The cursor advances by the small declared size, allowing subsequent records to reinterpret and copy overlapping bytes. POLYGON, POLYPOLYGON and POLYLINE share the same missing record-local boundary.

findings.remediation: Parse each WMF record exclusively through a slice of its declared extent, validate count-derived payload lengths before allocation, and impose aggregate retained-text and operation budgets.

limitations: No hostile WMF construction or application execution.
Exact memory and timing thresholds unmeasured.
validation.summary: Parent checked a nonzero placeable bounding box reaches raster_wmf. A short TEXTOUT record with a large u16 text count can read following records, provided trailing bytes cover its text/coordinates. ansi_text materializes owned nonblank Strings before any later failure. The 384-pixel canvas cap bounds raster dimensions, not retained text or record work. Rust whole-file bounds prevent a memory-safety read beyond the input, but do not enforce record framing.

findings.title: Rendering repeated embedded-font aliases can exhaust process memory
findings.summary: A DOCX font table can assign many distinct unknown family names to one internal font. Rendering eagerly copies and retains the entire font for each alias/style, multiplying memory far beyond admitted package bytes.

severity.rationale: Document-controlled aliases cause process memory exhaustion. Valid font bytes and recipient rendering are required; no remote or shared-service deployment is established.
severity.changeConditions: Per-worker memory quotas contain the impact; shared processing without isolation increases operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified aliases are retained separately, full copying precedes Arc ownership and font loading is eager. No runtime memory measurement.

codeEvidence.label: Eager embedded font loading
codeEvidence.explanation: The shared layout pipeline loads embedded fonts before actual face-use selection.

codeEvidence.label: Embedded font aliases
codeEvidence.explanation: Document font entries preserve their relationship/key under each supplied family name.

codeEvidence.label: Copy before deobfuscation
codeEvidence.explanation: Each alias copies the complete part, even if it is already a plain font.

codeEvidence.label: Independent alias retention
codeEvidence.explanation: Each noncatalogue alias/style resolves bytes, copies/validates them and retains its own allocation.

rootCause.summary: load_font_table preserves distinct document family names and embed relationships. load_embedded_fonts iterates every family/style; each invocation of deobfuscate_odttf allocates bytes.to_vec before validating the font and placing the allocation under its alias key. Shared ownership introduced afterward does not deduplicate the original part across aliases. No aggregate retained-font budget is enforced.

findings.remediation: Intern decoded fonts by resolved part identity and effective deobfuscation key before copying, share that allocation among aliases, and enforce an aggregate retained-font budget; load only needed faces where possible.

limitations: No font fixture or alias-heavy document was constructed or executed.
Allocation thresholds and host quotas unmeasured.
validation.summary: Parent verified the unconditional with_layout call and per-alias copying. An attacker can choose unique noncatalogue family names referencing the same valid plain font to bypass the installed-family optimization. Font validity checks constrain font syntax, while input byte budgets charge the single ZIP part rather than every retained copy. A large valid font plus aliases can demand multiple gigabytes.

dataflow.summary: Document font table -> family/style aliases -> same package part -> bytes.to_vec per alias -> independent retained font allocations
dataflow.source: Document-controlled font families and embedded-font relationships
dataflow.outcome: Memory amplification and potential process termination

likelihood.why: Repeated internal references are supported and no aggregate budget/deduplication is present.

reachability.summary: Public render/layout APIs eagerly call load_embedded_fonts before checking which faces the content actually uses.

attackPath.summary: Supply one valid embedded font and many distinct font-table aliases referencing it, then induce rendering.

remediationTests: Many aliases to one part share a single allocation or refuse at a fixed aggregate budget.
Distinct deobfuscation keys remain distinct; malformed font programs still refuse.

findings.title: Malformed HTML ampersands can stall DOCX rendering and Markdown conversion
findings.summary: For each ampersand, the HTML entity helper scans the entire remaining string for a semicolon, then advances one byte on failure. Repeated malformed ampersands cause quadratic CPU work in DOCX altChunks and Markdown raw HTML.

severity.rationale: Small enough input to pass ordinary byte limits can monopolize a processing worker. This is process availability impact without demonstrated remote service exposure.
severity.changeConditions: CPU timeouts and isolated workers constrain impact; repeated requests to an unisolated shared host raise operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified the full-suffix search precedes the intended length limit, one-byte failure progress and both consumer families; timing unmeasured.

codeEvidence.explanation: The document controls the internal HTML passed to the converter.

        let collapsed = collapse_ws(&decode_entities(raw));
codeEvidence.explanation: Raw HTML text enters decode_entities without XML entity restrictions.

codeEvidence.explanation: The ten-byte entity limit is tested only after searching the entire suffix.

codeEvidence.explanation: HTML block text also reaches the same decoder before text normalization.

rootCause.summary: decode_entities searches tail.find(';') before applying e <= 10. For strings containing many ampersands and no semicolon, every failed iteration scans almost all remaining bytes and consumes only one ampersand. Builder::text and Markdown HTML attributes/block text all reuse this helper. The bound limits accepted entity lengths, not search work.

findings.remediation: Bound the candidate entity prefix before searching for a semicolon, using a short byte iterator or UTF-8-safe slice, and keep linear failure progress.

limitations: No application execution or timing workload.
validation.summary: Parent confirmed consecutive raw ampersands repeatedly take the full-search/failure branch. Raw altChunk HTML is package-contained content, not the ordinary XML text checked for valid references. Markdown Event::Html content reaches html_block_text; html_attribute also calls the helper. The baseline rejection of a separate xmllinq unescape_xml_text hypothesis therefore does not reject this distinct helper/path.

dataflow.summary: Raw HTML -> altChunk Builder::text or Markdown HTML helpers -> decode_entities -> repeated unbounded semicolon suffix searches

likelihood.why: Malformed ampersands are sufficient and need no host configuration changes.

findings.title: A DTD inside an admitted DOCX can bypass XML depth limits and overflow the parser stack
findings.summary: Package admission ignores DTD events, but the later permissive DOM parser skips declarations only to the first greater-than sign. Nested markup hidden in an unused quoted DTD entity is then recursively parsed, bypassing the configured XML-depth bound.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can terminate an embedding process through stack exhaustion. High likelihood with process-availability impact is medium under the scan severity policy; baseline's high rating was recalibrated because no broader compromise or deployed shared service is established.
severity.changeConditions: Process isolation limits failure to a worker; availability-critical shared hosting could increase operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified admission dispatch, lazy DOM entry, declaration-skipping differential, recursive sink and the installed quick-xml 0.42 DTD tokenizer. No runtime crash reproduction.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled recursion through XML parser differential

codeEvidence.label: Public document admission
codeEvidence.explanation: Untrusted package bytes are admitted before being retained for lazy DOM parsing.

codeEvidence.label: Admission token handling
codeEvidence.explanation: Depth is checked for element events; DocType falls through Ok(_) with no rejection.

codeEvidence.label: Lazy main-document parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: The admitted main XML later enters the permissive parser.

codeEvidence.label: Declaration ends at first greater-than
codeEvidence.explanation: Declaration skipping is not aware of internal subsets or quoted entity values.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded element recursion
codeEvidence.explanation: Markup exposed from inside the declaration recursively invokes parse_element.

codeEvidence.label: Checked API rejects DTDs
codeEvidence.explanation: The strict validator explicitly rejects DTD declarations, unlike package admission.

rootCause.summary: WmlDocument::from_bytes admits XML using quick-xml depth events and retains its bytes. Package check_xml_depth ignores DocType. quick-xml's DTD tokenizer keeps a complete internal subset and quoted ENTITY value inside that event. When main_document later calls parse_xdocument, parse_document advances only to the first '>' of each declaration, exposing tag-like data inside the entity value. parse_element then recurses without enforcing the admitted depth limit.

findings.remediation: Reject DocType in package admission consistently with validate_xml, and make declaration skipping subset/quote aware or enforce parser recursion bounds as defense in depth.

limitations: No application execution, adversarial input generation or measured stack threshold.
Unchecked parse_xdocument intentionally lacks policy; finding is the package admission differential, not unchecked API availability.
validation.method: independent static source and dependency trace
validation.summary: Parent traced a DTD containing an inner ELEMENT declaration followed by an unused quoted ENTITY value holding many nested tags. Admission sees no corresponding Start events for those tags; the permissive parser skips past the inner ELEMENT and first apparent tag, then treats the remaining tags as elements. The actual local quick-xml 0.42 parser uses quote-sensitive DTD handling. Checked validate_xml rejects DocType, but WmlDocument's admission/lazy parsing path does not call that strict validator.

dataflow.summary: DOCX XML -> admission ignores DocType -> retained main part -> first-'>' declaration skip -> exposed nested tags -> recursive parse_element
dataflow.outcome: Stack overflow/process termination or WASM trap

impact.why: Process availability loss; no memory corruption/code execution established.

likelihood.why: Default depth policy misses the DTD text later reinterpreted as nested markup.

reachability.summary: Public WmlDocument::from_bytes followed by main_document is sufficient; original byte budgets allow deeply nested DTD text well below the maximum.

attackPath.summary: Supply an otherwise readable DOCX whose main XML starts with a DTD containing deeply nested tag text in an unused entity value, then induce lazy main-document parsing.

remediationTests: Deep tag text inside an unused DTD entity returns INVALID_XML before DOM construction.
Checked and package admission APIs consistently reject DTD declarations.

A well-formed main XML prefixed by ' and matching '' then ">]> hides all nested tags inside a DTD entity value from quick-xml's depth scan. Permissive parser skips to ELEMENT's >, then skips to first 's > inside ENTITY, then recurses into remaining '' tags, causing stack overflow before document root. WmlDocument::from_bytes admission (src/wml_document.rs:50-58) -> main_document parse_xdocument (94-102) gives supported entry point. Strict validate_xml rejects DTD but WmlDocument route uses admission and unchecked parse. Verifying dependency DocType scanning statically now; no code execution.

findings.title: Conflicting ZIP footer counts bypass the archive entry limit
findings.summary: Admission checks the ZIP32 total-entry field, while zip 9.0.5 indexes using entries-on-this-disk. A positive small total with a larger on-disk count bypasses max_entries, and no post-open upper-bound check repairs the mismatch.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document bypasses an explicit allocation/work budget and forces significantly more indexed/processed parts, including a caller-selected low cap. Other byte budgets still apply; no code execution or unbounded ZIP32 count is claimed.
severity.changeConditions: Low custom entry caps make the relative bypass larger; strict process quotas constrain availability impact. ZIP32's u16 count and independent byte limits remain bounds.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified both EOCD field consumers, normal positive-count footer lookup and one-sided archive.len check in current source/dependency. No runtime reproduction.

taxonomy.category: Resource limit bypass through inconsistent archive metadata

codeEvidence.label: Declared count admission
codeEvidence.explanation: Only the helper's chosen count is checked against max_entries before indexing.

codeEvidence.label: ZIP32 total field selection
codeEvidence.explanation: The helper selects total entries at EOCD offset ten without reconciling entries-on-disk.

codeEvidence.label: One-sided post-index check
codeEvidence.explanation: The post-open check detects undercounts caused by duplicate names, not counts above the budget.

codeEvidence.label: PartFs loading
codeEvidence.explanation: PartFs repeats the same precheck then processes every indexed entry without an actual count cap.

codeEvidence.label: Pinned ZIP implementation
codeEvidence.code:
[[package]]
name = "zip"
version = "9.0.5"
source = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"
checksum = "6e04976da629d3b04204ba8105b396a193af8ad2583b2c79bfb3ab8af580a11e"
codeEvidence.explanation: The current lockfile selects zip 9.0.5, whose ZIP32 index uses entries-on-this-disk.

rootCause.summary: preindex_budget reads declared_entry_count and compares it with max_entries. For ZIP32 the helper trusts EOCD total entries at +10. The installed zip reader instead uses entries-on-this-disk at +8 to govern index construction. admit only rejects archive.len smaller than declared, and PartFs read_package has no actual-count upper bound. Contradictory metadata therefore crosses the entry-count admission control.

findings.remediation: Before indexing reconcile and bound every applicable ZIP32/ZIP64 count used by the reader, reject contradictory single-disk counts, and independently enforce archive.len <= max_entries after open in admission and PartFs loading.

limitations: No malformed ZIP was generated or executed.
Compressed, per-part and total inflation budgets and ZIP32 count width remain effective.
validation.method: independent static source and dependency trace
validation.summary: Parent checked zip 9.0.5 read/mod.rs:68-74 selecting on-disk count, format/blocks.rs:329-360 preserving both fields without equality validation, format/find_central_directory.rs:145-213 using regular lookup for positive total, and read/zip_archive.rs:271-299 consuming the selected count. Use total=1 rather than the original candidate's total=0: zero takes a special empty-archive branch. With valid distinct parts and on-disk count exceeding the budget, the application precheck and one-sided postcheck do not refuse the excess.

dataflow.summary: EOCD +10 -> preindex_budget passes; EOCD +8 -> zip indexing -> archive.len processing without max_entries upper bound
dataflow.sink: Archive indexing and per-entry package loading
dataflow.outcome: Caller/default entry-budget bypass and amplified work/memory

impact.why: Defeats a resource admission invariant and increases processing resource use.

likelihood.why: Contradictory ZIP32 counts are not reconciled at either application consumer.

reachability.summary: Public admission and PartFs loading consume supplied archive bytes; neither requires host configuration control.
reachability.outcome: Processing more archive entries than authorized

attackPath.summary: Supply a ZIP32 DOCX with genuine central/local entries, total entries set to one and a larger entries-on-disk count, then request admission or loading.

remediationTests: An archive with total=1 and on-disk count above max_entries refuses before indexing.
Post-open count enforcement protects both admission and PartFs.
Normal agreeing counts and ZIP64 limits retain expected behavior.

Set +10=0, +8=actual 60000; sole post-open check archive.len()<declared at admission.rs:451 accepts actual>budget. read_package:282-285 repeats preindex without actual count bound. Structural archive/inflation/names can remain valid. Upstream footer parse reads both counts; central-directory finder check pending. Static only.
originalCandidate.refinement: Baseline and parent corrected total=0 to total=1 because the dependency special-cases empty archives.

surfaces.label: DOCX altChunk HTML numeric expansion
surfaces.notes: Validated at src/convert/altchunk.rs:562-566,469-490 after admission src/convert/mod.rs:773-798. Archive admission and host process limits do not bound generated columns.

surfaces.label: WMF record-local payload boundaries
surfaces.notes: Parent validated whole-file payload reads at src/convert/metafile.rs:603-684 and owned text retention at 692-700. Canvas clipping, checked size multiplication and EMF record-local bounds do not repair the WMF framing flaw.

surfaces.label: DTD admission versus permissive DOM tokenization
surfaces.notes: Parent validated src/admission.rs:795-820 ignoring DTD, src/wml_document.rs:50-96 lazy unchecked parsing and src/xmllinq/parse.rs:539-548,660-663 recursion. Strict validation rejects DTD at 954 but is absent from the affected package path. Baseline high severity recalibrated to medium for process DoS.

surfaces.label: Embedded font alias retention
surfaces.notes: Parent validated eager copies at src/convert/font_table.rs:179-193,205-231 and src/convert/mod.rs:806-808. Catalogue skipping and font syntax validation do not limit aggregate alias-created memory.

surfaces.label: HTML entity decoding complexity
surfaces.notes: Parent validated src/convert/altchunk.rs:728-759 and Markdown consumers src/markdown/write.rs:1357,1420. Distinct from baseline's rejected ordinary XML decoder candidate, where quick-xml reference validation provides counterevidence.

surfaces.label: ZIP footer count resource admission
surfaces.notes: Validated conflicting count selection at src/admission.rs:399-407,590-601 and unbounded actual entry processing at src/opc/mod.rs:282-289. Current zip 9.0.5 uses ZIP32 entries-on-disk. The original total=0 example was corrected to total=1 due the dependency empty-archive branch.

surfaces.label: Source-embedded credentials and private keys
surfaces.notes: Independent baseline searched current hidden/configuration/documentation/test/example/inactive source for provider tokens, private-key headers, bearer/JWTs, credential URLs and assignments. No credential disclosure candidate found. tests/self_update_signature.rs uses explicitly deterministic throwaway signing seeds; workflow references use secret stores. Current release key list is empty. Git history and live credential validation were not used.

surfaces.label: Ordinary XML entity-decoding complexity hypothesis
surfaces.notes: Baseline original hypothesis concerned malformed ampersand runs reaching xmllinq unescape_xml_text. Source counterevidence: actual quick-xml rejects malformed references before ordinary package text reaches that path; strict XML handling at src/xmllinq/parse.rs:930-965 also refuses unsupported references. This rejection does not apply to the separately reported raw HTML helper at src/convert/altchunk.rs:728-759. No candidate finding was dropped.

surfaces.label: Unrestricted individual image decode hypothesis
surfaces.notes: The hypothesis that image::load_from_memory disables all allocation limits is rejected: Cargo.lock:1307-1310 selects image 0.25.10; its ImageReader::decode reserves decoder.total_bytes against default Limits.max_alloc=512 MiB. Local dependency src/io/image_reader_type.rs:311-322 and src/io/limits.rs:33-55 verified. The limit is not a conversion-wide budget; later RGB/RGBA copies/source pixmaps and aggregate repeated references remain a specific follow-up, not a proven extra finding.

surfaces.label: MCP root containment and native filesystem publication
surfaces.notes: Full audit of jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py, src/publication.rs and supporting PyOutputRoot at jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278 confirms reads/writes use a retained cap-std directory capability. Relative output policy rejects traversal/nonportable names; staging is exclusive, no-overwrite hard-link commit prevents conflict races, overwrite renames the link rather than following referents. Native publish_paths separately grants ambient caller-selected parent authority. Sets are atomic per file, with partial commits/durability errors reported; no set-wide atomicity claimed.

surfaces.label: Native Markdown resource reads and external relationships
surfaces.notes: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2878 decodes escapes, rejects schemes, canonicalizes into caller-selected root and performs capability-relative image reads. Internal media/font relationships use PartFs::part_bytes, not host or network fetch. Cargo.toml image features omit SVG. src/convert/font.rs:2228-2236 restricts cloud-family names to one normal component. No document-controlled external fetch or arbitrary host-file read established in inspected paths.

surfaces.label: Native updater signature and extracted-binary controls
surfaces.notes: Full src/update.rs review verifies explicit command/confirmation, fixed repository/platform/tag, checksum configuration and extracted regular-file hook. RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None intentionally leave signatures disabled, consistent with docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80. Archive-plus-checksum replacement requires publisher-level release-asset control; no lower-trust document-to-update path established. Signature absence alone is not promoted as an exploit. Dependency internals and deployment tag/account protection remain unverified.

surfaces.label: WMF/EMF canvas and coordinate-span bounds
surfaces.notes: Reviewed controls in src/convert/metafile.rs include MAX_SIDE=384, clipped stroke walks/widths, clamped fill scanlines and record-local EMF point bounds at 1061-1082. These reject the straightforward unbounded-canvas/coordinate-span hypotheses but do not repair the reported WMF payload boundary flaw.

surfaces.label: MCP root documentation versus font/cache resources
surfaces.notes: Preserved discrepancy: mcp_server.py:5-9,67-108 says tools only touch root, while rendering accesses system/user fonts and src/convert/font.rs:3098-3107,3154-3229 reads/writes a configured ambient font index. Parent verified platform roots, JUBARTE_FONT_DIR, index override/empty-off and complete derived default parent(font-root)/font-index.tsv. No arbitrary document-only file capability established; local cache tampering requires separate writable-directory/index authority. Root enforcement applies to document I/O, not a process sandbox.

surfaces.label: Whole-scope source coverage reconciliation
surfaces.notes: Selected current inventory contains 2900 paths. Fully audited union contains 12 files: SECURITY.md, src/admission.rs, src/opc/archive.rs, src/xmllinq/parse.rs, src/wml_document.rs, src/lib.rs, tests/self_update_signature.rs, src/convert/font_table.rs, src/publication.rs, src/update.rs, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py, src/convert/altchunk.rs. All remaining 2888 paths are retained explicitly under scope-review-remainder; architecture mapping/search-only inspections are not full coverage.

surfaces.label: CI cache and runner deployment controls
surfaces.notes: Architecture follow-up found public PR code on self-hosted runners and an unauthenticated private-network cache URL, but actual cache write authorization/protocol and runner isolation are not in this repository. Preserve uncertainty rather than asserting cache poisoning.

surfaces.label: Authentication, tenants and privileged caller-only options
surfaces.notes: The inspected product is an in-process library/local CLI and stdio MCP. No hosted tenant service was supplied. Inside-root MCP overwrite=true, ambient operator-selected CLI output paths and permissive low-level parser options are already-granted capabilities; absence of web authentication or human approval is not independently reported.

deferred.reason: Whole-repository source review remains incomplete. Complete file-level security audit of these actual current in-scope paths; prioritize remaining comparison/edit/Markdown/legacy/native-binding implementations and generated WASM implementations. This terminal worker result preserves the gap instead of claiming complete coverage.
Validate conversion-wide repeated media allocations and later RGB/RGBA/pixmap copies beyond the dependency per-decode budget; no extra vulnerability promoted without parent proof.

Establish actual self-hosted runner lifetime/network isolation and mbx server write authorization; delegated action/server implementation is absent from authorized source. No confirmed cache-poisoning finding.

openQuestions: Whole-scope audit is incomplete: only the explicitly fully reviewed files were counted. The retained scope-review-remainder task lists every other current in-scope path; selective source traces and broad search matches were not counted as full review.

Aggregate image decoding/retention and later RGB/RGBA/tiny-skia allocations need further review. A 512 MiB per-decode dependency limit does not establish a conversion-wide budget (src/convert/mod.rs:18401-18403,27551-27577; src/convert/raster.rs:383-425,559). No separate extra vulnerability is asserted.

Self-hosted CI/docs execute repository source, and .github/actions/mbx/action.yml points at http://mbx-cache:7543 with no client token. Comments claim PR read-only cache publication, but server-side authorization, runner lifetime/isolation and trusted-branch publishing controls are absent here. Source alone does not establish cache poisoning or private-network compromise.

Third-party Jules action internals, actual permissions/installation, release/tag/account protection, registry authorization and actual signing-secret provisioning were not available in the authorized repository; these remain deployment prerequisites.

Native renderer font/cache ambient I/O is broader than the blanket MCP root wording; reconcile documentation or decide whether host-level sandboxing is required. No document-only arbitrary file access was established.
No hostile inputs were executed. Crash thresholds, performance/memory measurements and platform-specific runtime behavior remain unmeasured; findings were validated against source.

Transient execution recovery retained the saved draft/model/findings. The earlier architecture follow-up emitted partial host/CI conclusions before the transient failure; no child remains active and no replacement agent was spawned.
